questions.question: After ditching in water, passengers and crewmembers should wait to inflate their life vests until they have exited the aircraft.
questions.explanation: An inflated life vest can trap you against the ceiling if the cabin floods, so you inflate it only after you're out of the aircraft.

questions.question: The APG or RWA Analysis will specify an altitude for acceleration and clean up from second segment to final segment climb speed/configuration.
questions.explanation: "The APG or RWA Analysis will specify an altitude for acceleration and clean up from second segment to final segment climb speed/configuration."

questions.question: Prior to each departure during IMC, crewmembers will obtain and review the appropriate APG or RWA airport obstacle analysis and aircraft performance information pertinent to the airport and runway of intended use to determine the takeoff weight limit for the aircraft to satisfy OEI obstacle clearance requirements.
questions.explanation: Before an IMC departure you review the obstacle analysis to find the max takeoff weight that still clears obstacles on one engine.

questions.question: The takeoff weight must be limited so as not to exceed any brake energy limitation for the flight.
questions.explanation: Takeoff weight also has to stay under the brakes' maximum energy limit so a rejected takeoff won't overheat or fail the brakes.

questions.question: All Company flights will be required to ensure obstacle avoidance for every flight regardless whether the flight is operated under Part 91, Part 91K, or Part 135. As a general rule the methods for obstacle avoidance and analysis are:

choices.c: APG or RWA data.

questions.explanation: The company's obstacle-avoidance methods are APG/RWA analysis (IMC), see-and-avoid in VMC, and special visual procedures at mountain airports — of the choices, APG/RWA data is the one listed.

questions.question: If contaminated runway data exists (approved or non-approved) for the aircraft, it will be used to determine required runway for departure and landing on contaminated runways.
questions.explanation: "When the runway for departure is wet or contaminated, takeoff weight will be limited by applicable wet/contaminated AFM supplemental performance data, APG, or RWA."

questions.question: Crews are authorized to accept and fly RNAV Q Routes.
questions.explanation: Q routes (high-altitude RNAV routes) are authorized.

questions.question: Prior to using GPS based navigation systems crews must verify that RAIM is available.
questions.explanation: You must confirm RAIM (GPS integrity monitoring) is available before relying on GPS navigation.

questions.question: When cleared for an RNAV departure, crews must ensure that the following is correctly loaded in the navigation system...

choices.b: The first fix, and the first altitude.
choices.c: The current version of the cleared RNAV procedure and the first fix.
choices.d: The current version of the cleared RNAV procedure, the take-off runway, and the assigned transition.

questions.answer_text: The current version of the cleared RNAV procedure, the take-off runway, and the assigned transition.
questions.explanation: For an RNAV departure you load the current cleared procedure, the takeoff runway, and the assigned transition — not just the first fix.

questions.question: Pilot crewmembers will receive an updated weather briefing within 30 minutes prior to landing at the destination.
questions.explanation: You get an updated weather briefing within 30 minutes of landing.

questions.question: When flying RNAV departures and arrivals, manually selecting bank limiting (half bank) may reduce ability to satisfy ATC path expectations.
questions.explanation: Half-bank can keep the airplane from turning tightly enough to stay on the RNAV path ATC expects.

questions.question: Government charts (NACO) are not authorized. Jeppesen charts that are provided on the EFBs must be used for all passenger carrying operations.
questions.explanation: The FOM allows Jeppesen OR NACO charts when paper is required, so NACO isn't prohibited — the statement is false.

questions.question: When are you prohibited from accepting a “line up and wait” clearance?

choices.a: At night with visibility less than 1 mile and the departure runway is being used only for departures.
choices.b: A line up and wait clearance is not authorized
choices.c: Night or day with visibility less than 1 mile, unless the crew can be assured that the departure runway is not being used for arrivals.

questions.answer_text: Night or day with visibility less than 1 mile, unless the crew can be assured that the departure runway is not being used for arrivals.
questions.explanation: You can't accept 'line up and wait' day or night with visibility under 1 mile unless you're sure the runway isn't being used for arrivals.

questions.question: Unless otherwise stated in the notes section in Tailwinds, visual approaches from sunset to sunrise are only authorized at airports that are served by...

choices.a: A VASI/PAPI or a precision approach.
choices.c: An Instrument approach with Category D circling minimums

questions.answer_text: An Instrument approach with Category D circling minimums
questions.explanation: At night, visual approaches are only allowed at airports served by an instrument approach with Category D circling minimums.

questions.question: Airports that have specific restrictions will be found…

choices.b: In the Jeppesen General Airway Manual.
choices.c: In the notes section in Tailwinds and in the Additional Airport Information folder in ForeFlight.

questions.answer_text: In the notes section in Tailwinds and in the Additional Airport Information folder in ForeFlight.
questions.explanation: Airport-specific restrictions are in the Tailwinds notes and the ForeFlight Additional Airport Information folder.

questions.question: When the autopilot is engaged the PF will make and verbalize changes on the flight director panel.
questions.explanation: "When the autopilot is engaged the PF will make and verbalize changes on the flight director panel."

questions.question: If a visual approach is planned to a runway that is served by a precision IAP, the crew is required to have that approach tuned and displayed on the navigation unit and shall use the navigation information to correctly identify the intended airport and runway.
questions.explanation: The crew "is required to have that approach tuned and displayed on the navigation unit and shall use the navigation information to correctly identify the intended airport and runway."

questions.question: Pilots are authorized to conduct contact approaches.
questions.explanation: Contact approaches are not authorized, so the statement is false.

questions.question: Which document(s) contain information regarding operations during ground icing conditions?

choices.c: CFM

questions.explanation: "Ops Spec A041 requires a pre-takeoff contamination check whenever operating in ground icing conditions" — covered in FOM Section 7, Ops Spec A041, and the CFM.

questions.question: As part of the post de-icing inspection, the crew must verify that which of the following items are free of frozen contaminants?

choices.a: Aircraft critical surfaces, and all pitot/static ports.
choices.b: Engine inlets and inlet protection devices, main and nose gear wells.
choices.c: Cabin/baggage doors, and verify flight control unrestricted full range of movement.

questions.explanation: "Check all critical surfaces are free of frozen contaminants" — all of the listed items must be verified in the post-deicing inspection.

questions.question: A Pre-Takeoff Contamination Check will be conducted whenever...

choices.a: operations are conducted with visibility less than 2 SM.
choices.b: ground icing conditions exist and hold over time has been exceeded.
choices.c: ground icing conditions exist, and you have used a Type IV anti-ice fluid.

questions.explanation: "Ops Spec A041 requires a pre-takeoff contamination check whenever operating in ground icing conditions."

questions.question: A tactile pre-takeoff contamination check will be conducted...

choices.a: during preflight when ground icing conditions exist.
choices.c: before takeoff when the crew is unable to determine that aircraft surfaces are free from contamination using a visual check.
choices.d: before takeoff with freezing drizzle or light freezing rain.

questions.answer_text: before takeoff when the crew is unable to determine that aircraft surfaces are free from contamination using a visual check.
questions.explanation: A tactile (hands-on) check is done before takeoff when you can't confirm the surfaces are clean just by looking. (Kept per FOM; the official key marks e.)

questions.question: When conducting operations in ground icing conditions, holdover timetables are only required to be referenced if using a Type IV anti-ice solution.
questions.explanation: "The use of holdover times is for reference only and may not be solely relied upon to determine if the aircraft surfaces are free of contamination" — so it isn't only for Type IV. False.

questions.question: You have determined that a Pre-Takeoff Contamination Check must be conducted. When must the check be completed?

choices.b: Within 10 minutes prior to beginning takeoff.
choices.c: Prior to taxi.
choices.d: Within 5 minutes prior to beginning takeoff.

questions.answer_text: Within 5 minutes prior to beginning takeoff.
questions.explanation: The contamination check is done "within 5 minutes prior to beginning takeoff."

questions.question: Winter operations information is found in which source document(s)?

choices.c: FOM section 4

questions.explanation: Winter/weather operations are in FOM Section 7.

questions.question: The preferred fluids for anti-icing are...

choices.c: Type I, II, and IV
choices.d: Type I, II, III and IV

questions.explanation: "The preferred fluids for anti-icing are Type II and IV."

questions.question: What can be said about de-ice/anti-ice fluids?

choices.a: De-icing fluids are used to remove frozen contaminants from aircraft critical surfaces.
choices.b: Anti-icing fluids should be applied in a uniform layer and in sufficient quantity until it starts to flow off the aircraft surfaces.
choices.c: The preferred fluids for anti-icing are Type II and IV.
choices.d: All the above statements are true.

questions.answer_text: All the above statements are true.
questions.explanation: "De-icing fluids are used to remove frozen contaminants from aircraft critical surfaces" — all three statements are true.

questions.question: We are prohibited from departing during ground icing conditions, if our holdover time (HOT) has been exceeded.
questions.explanation: "Unless it can be positively determined that the aircraft surfaces are free of contamination immediately prior to takeoff (within five minutes), the crew may need to repeat the de/anti-ice process or delay" — an expired HOT alone doesn't ground you. False.

questions.question: When does holdover time begin on a 2 step de-ice/anti-ice?

choices.a: At the end of the final application of de-ice/anti-ice fluid.
choices.b: At the beginning of the first application of de-ice/anti-ice fluid.
choices.c: When the final application of de-icing/anti-icing fluid commences.

questions.answer_text: When the final application of de-icing/anti-icing fluid commences.
questions.explanation: "HOT begins when the final application of de-icing/anti-icing fluid commences."

questions.question: It is acceptable to polish frost smooth using something such as a rag or paper prior to departure.
questions.explanation: "'Polishing' frost smooth and conducting a takeoff is prohibited. Frost must be removed as any other frozen contaminant."

questions.question: When conducting a night arrival into KEGE, crews may only use runway 25 and must use the LDA/DME RWY 25 or RNAV Y RWY 25 approach. The PAPI and GS must be operational.
questions.explanation: At night into Eagle you may use only Runway 25 via the LDA DME or RNAV Y RWY 25, and the PAPI and glideslope must be working.

questions.question: A high minimums PIC may not use lower than standard takeoff minimums authorized in Op Spec C079.
questions.explanation: A high-minimums PIC can't use the lower-than-standard takeoff minimums from Ops Spec C079.

questions.question: If ATC does not specify any other particular departure procedure prior to takeoff, a crewmember must comply with the departure procedure established by the FAA for the airport and runway to be used.
questions.explanation: If ATC doesn't specify a departure procedure, you fly the FAA-published DP/ODP for obstacle clearance.

questions.question: When a filed flight plan has been amended within 30 minutes of scheduled departure time by either Flight Planning or the flight crew, it is the flight crew’s responsibility to advise ATC/FSS of the possibility of two flight plans on file. When a change has occurred within 30 minutes of scheduled departure, the flight crew must request a full route clearance from ATC/FSS.
questions.explanation: If the flight plan changes within 30 minutes of departure, tell ATC/FSS about the possible duplicate and request a full route clearance.

questions.question: If ATC issues an instruction that is contrary to a TCAS RA, you must comply with ATC’s instructions.
questions.explanation: You follow the TCAS RA over a conflicting ATC instruction — "Respond immediately to any 'increase' or 'reversal' RA maneuver advisories." False.

questions.question: When conducting a visual approach, the multi-function display (MFD), if available, should be continuously adjusted to the lowest scale which allows the destination airport to remain visible.
questions.explanation: On a visual, keep the moving map at the lowest scale that still shows the destination airport.

questions.question: For destination airport planning a grooved/porous runway can be considered effectively dry when the forecast for precipitation at the estimated time of arrival is less than moderate.
questions.explanation: "A grooved/porous runway can be considered effectively dry when the forecast for precipitation at the estimated time of arrival is less than moderate."

questions.question: What is the minimum length of available runway necessary for land and hold short operations (LAHSO)?

choices.b: The minimum runway length required in the aircraft CFM.
choices.c: When the hold short point is near the end of a very long runway.
choices.d: The Company is not authorized to conduct land and hold short operations.

questions.answer_text: The Company is not authorized to conduct land and hold short operations.
questions.explanation: The company is not authorized to conduct land-and-hold-short (LAHSO) at any airport.

questions.question: When more than 25 percent of the runway surface area (whether in isolated areas or not) within the required length and width being used is covered by standing water, snow (dry or wet), loose snow, compacted snow, slush or ice (including wet ice), the runway is considered to be...

choices.c: Contaminated

questions.explanation: "A runway is contaminated when more than 25 percent of the runway... is covered by standing water, snow, loose snow, compacted snow, slush or ice."

questions.question: DAAP restrictions include... the runway must have an approved and operational visual guidance system or serviced by an operational glide slope (i.e., ILS, LPV, LNAV/VNAV, FMS Visual with VGP) unless a DAAP exception has been granted.
questions.explanation: DAAP requires an operational visual guidance system or glideslope unless a DAAP exception is granted — the statement is true.

questions.question: Which of the following conditions precludes the use of DAAP?

choices.a: Light turbulence is reported on final approach.
choices.c: The runway has loose snow.

questions.explanation: Inoperative anti-skid rules out DAAP — anti-skid must be operational.

questions.question: Under what limitation may company pilots file to, and begin an instrument approach procedure to, an airport that does not have a weather reporting facility?

choices.a: The weather at the intended destination must be at least 1000/3.
choices.b: The airport must have an operational control tower.
choices.c: An alternate airport is filed that has a weather reporting facility.
choices.d: You must first contact the FODM on duty.

questions.answer_text: An alternate airport is filed that has a weather reporting facility.
questions.explanation: As an Eligible On-Demand operator you may start an approach to an airport with no weather reporting if you file an alternate that does have weather reporting.

questions.question: The PM typically enters data which should be confirmed with the PF before activation. The Confirm, Activate, Monitor and Intervene (CAMI) procedure shall be used to assure desired outcomes whenever interfacing with automation systems.
questions.explanation: CAMI (Confirm, Activate, Monitor, Intervene) is the procedure used when working with the automation.

questions.question: Which is false with regards to entering a runway (active or non-active) for the purpose of crossing or positioning for takeoff?

choices.a: The anti-collision light must be turned on.
choices.b: Both pilots must hear and understand the taxi clearance and verbally agree before crossing any hold short line.
choices.c: Both pilots must be task free.
choices.d: Checklists and FBO communications may be accomplished during runway crossing.

questions.answer_text: Checklists and FBO communications may be accomplished during runway crossing.
questions.explanation: The false statement is that checklists/FBO comms may be done during a runway crossing — both pilots must be task-free. (Kept per FOM; the official key marks b.)

questions.question: When using a marshaller/wing walker, what is the minimum distance we must maintain from an obstacle/aircraft?

choices.c: 15 feet.
choices.d: There is no minimum distance. Just use caution when being marshaled in by the line personnel.

questions.explanation: Even with a wing-walker you never taxi under your own power within 5 feet of another aircraft or obstacle.

questions.question: When NOT using a marshaller/wing walker, what is the minimum distance we must maintain from an obstacle/aircraft?

choices.c: 15 feet.

questions.explanation: Without a marshaller/wing-walker you keep at least 10 feet — under 10 feet you're required to use one.

questions.question: When conditions at the destination or alternate require the use of the 80% rule for landing, an SIC with less than 100 hours in type may make the landing when...

choices.a: Visibility is less than ¾ of a mile.
choices.b: Braking action is less than good.
choices.c: Crosswind component is greater than 10 knots but less than 15 knots.
choices.d: Wind shear is reported at the airport.

questions.answer_text: Crosswind component is greater than 10 knots but less than 15 knots.
questions.explanation: A sub-100-hour SIC may still land with a 10–15 kt crosswind; it's a crosswind over 15 kt (or low vis, poor braking, windshear, contamination) that stops them.

questions.question: Hazardous materials may not be accepted for transport on company aircraft, but there are certain exceptions.
questions.explanation: Flexjet is a "Will Not Carry" hazmat certificate holder — hazmat isn't accepted except for the specific listed exceptions. True.

questions.question: Oxygen for medical use by passengers is allowed under specific conditions. Which statement regarding the carriage of oxygen is TRUE?”

choices.a: Compressed gas medical oxygen required for the duration of the flight, may be transported in the cabin of the aircraft.
choices.b: Because it is considered “for medical purposes”, liquid oxygen may be carried on Company aircraft.
choices.c: Recreational or flavored oxygen may be carried in containers of less than 20 ounces.
choices.d: Only approved portable oxygen concentrators (POCs) may be carried. Compressed gas medical oxygen may never be carried onboard company aircraft.

questions.answer_text: Only approved portable oxygen concentrators (POCs) may be carried. Compressed gas medical oxygen may never be carried onboard company aircraft.
questions.explanation: Only approved portable oxygen concentrators may be carried — compressed-gas and liquid medical oxygen are never allowed onboard.

questions.question: Flights under Part 91 and 91K will be conducted to the same standards as Part 135 operations except where noted in the FOM. Exceptions include...

choices.a: Passenger ID checks are not required.
choices.c: ETOPS 180 limitation does not apply.
choices.d: Direct communication with an air/ground communication facility per Ops Spec C077 does not apply.

questions.explanation: All of the listed Part 91/91K differences from Part 135 apply.

questions.question: When the crosswind, including gusts, at the destination airport exceeds the aircraft demonstrated crosswind, but less than the Landing Wind Limitations guidance in this section, an alternate airport will be selected or coordinated with Flight Planning by the PIC.
questions.explanation: When crosswind exceeds the demonstrated value but is below the limit, the PIC selects or coordinates an alternate with Flight Planning — the statement is true. (Kept per FOM; the official key marks False.)

questions.question: Section 4 of the FOM addresses all the policies and procedures regarding operational control.
questions.explanation: Section 4 is 'Flight Operations,' not operational control, so the statement is false.

questions.question: Winter operations guidance is located in FOM Section 7.
questions.explanation: Winter operations guidance is in FOM Section 7 — true.

questions.question: Operations Specifications authorize crews to conduct certain operations, while the Flight Operations Manual provides standard operating procedures, which allow Company personnel to carry out their duties and responsibilities in accordance with company policies, FAA regulations, Ops Specs, and M Specs.
questions.explanation: Ops Specs authorize what you're allowed to do; the FOM gives the standard procedures to do it — true.

questions.question: Although the Company may provide flight planning services for the crewmembers, the PIC is responsible for the accuracy, safety, and regulatory compliance of all facets of flight planning.
questions.explanation: Even when the company plans the flight, the PIC is responsible for its accuracy and legality — true.

questions.question: Crews are required to turn their aircraft’s anti-collision lights on while taxiing across a runway.
questions.explanation: Anti-collision lights go on when taxiing across a runway — true.

questions.question: Prior to engine start for each departure, the PIC will initiate the AWARE briefing.
questions.explanation: The PIC starts the AWARE briefing before engine start — true.

questions.question: The acronym AWARE stands for...

choices.a: Aircraft Status, Weather, Airport, Route verification, and Extras.
choices.b: Aircraft Status, Weather, Arrival, Runway, and Extras.
choices.c: Airport Status, Weather, Arrival, Route, and Emergency review.
choices.d: Airport, Weather, Aircraft, Runway, and Emergency exits.

questions.answer_text: Aircraft Status, Weather, Airport, Route verification, and Extras.
questions.explanation: AWARE = Aircraft status, Weather, Airport, Route verification, Extras.

questions.question: The following restrictions apply anytime crews are using the DAAP relief for preflight planning...

choices.a: Lift dump devices, if installed, must be operational.
choices.b: Thrust reversers, if installed, must be operational for operations on wet runways.
choices.c: Anti-skid, if installed, must be operational.
choices.d: The runway must have an approved and operational visual guidance system or serviced by an operational glide slope (i.e., ILS, LPV, LNAV/VNAV, FMS Visual with VGP) unless a DAAP exception has been granted.

questions.explanation: All of the listed DAAP restrictions apply.

questions.question: Company pilots may use DAAP in their pre-flight planning when the destination runway is contaminated.
questions.explanation: DAAP can be used into a contaminated destination as long as the runway is at least 115% of the length needed for a dry runway — so it's true.

questions.question: Prior to boarding the aircraft, the PIC will ensure __________ is completed.

choices.c: The Pre-Taxi Briefing

questions.explanation: Before boarding, the PIC makes sure a final walk-around is completed.

questions.question: Prior to the first flight on an aircraft during a PIC’s rotation and following any maintenance being performed during the rotation, the PIC will conduct a thorough review of the aircraft status book with the Maintenance Controller.
questions.explanation: At the start of a rotation and after any maintenance, the PIC reviews the aircraft status book with Maintenance Control — true.

questions.question: The PIC is the final authority in determining safe fuel loads. As safety allows he/she will follow the Fuel Guide recommendation as published on the flight plan located in the total fuel field (TOTL). If the PIC determines more or less fuel is required (greater than +/- ___ pounds), he/she must inform the Flight Planning Department of the changed fuel load with the applicable reason by either responding via email to the flight plan or by phone.
questions.explanation: If you need more or less fuel than the plan by more than ±200 lb, you must tell Flight Planning why.

questions.question: What is the maximum allowable gust factor for all flight operations according to the FOM?

choices.c: 25 kts.

questions.explanation: The maximum gust factor is 20 knots (15 for a high-minimums PIC).

questions.question: When computing a weight and balance, standard average weights, actual weights, or a combination of both weights shall be used per the guidance in…

choices.c: FOM Appendix 1.

questions.explanation: Weight-and-balance guidance (standard, actual, or combined weights) is in FOM Appendix 3. (Section 4.9.13's 'Appendix 1' reference is a typo — Appendix 1 has no W&B data.)

questions.question: You are scheduled to fly 3 legs, totaling 9.6 hours of flying. During the first leg of the day, due to circumstances outside of your control, it becomes apparent that you will exceed 10 hours of flying. According to our FOM are you legal to complete your flights?

choices.a: The crew can legally complete the remaining flights, provided the series of flights was realistically planned. The aircrew will be provided rest as required by 14 CFR, or otherwise required, prior to the next Duty Period if the total flight time exceeded the ten-hours.
choices.b: A flight crew may never exceed a 10-in-24 warning under any circumstance.
choices.c: The crew can legally complete the remaining flights provided the series of flights if the remaining legs are conducted under FAR Part 91.
choices.d: Flight crews can exceed 10 hours of flight time in 24 hours but never 14 hours of duty within a 24-hour period.

questions.answer_text: The crew can legally complete the remaining flights, provided the series of flights was realistically planned. The aircrew will be provided rest as required by 14 CFR, or otherwise required, prior to the next Duty Period if the total flight time exceeded the ten-hours.
questions.explanation: Legal if the flights were "realistically planned"; rest is then provided as required by 14 CFR before the next duty period.

questions.question: May you still operate a Part 135 flight if your passenger has forgotten their REAL ID?

choices.a: Yes, as long as they have an approved alternate form of Federal ID.
choices.b: Yes, ID’s are not required to be checked.
choices.c: Yes, you can call the Safety department and in very rare instances get a waiver for the passenger.

questions.answer_text: Yes, as long as they have an approved alternate form of Federal ID.
questions.explanation: On a Part 135 flight, a passenger without their REAL ID can still be identified with two other forms of ID, one of which is government-issued.

questions.question: While preparing for a flight, a maintenance discrepancy is found. Maintenance is notified and the item is deferred under the MEL but TAILWINDS still shows a Maintenance Alert. Which statement below is most accurate?

choices.a: You may depart as long as scheduling tells you it is ok.
choices.b: You may depart as long as the Maintenance Duty Manager sends you the required release via Tailwinds, email, or FAX stating that you are cleared to depart.
choices.c: You cannot depart.
choices.d: You can depart as long as the FODM sends you an email saying all items have been cleared.

questions.answer_text: You may depart as long as the Maintenance Duty Manager sends you the required release via Tailwinds, email, or FAX stating that you are cleared to depart.
questions.explanation: If a Tailwinds warning is present the PIC must "receive the following release via the Tailwinds App, email, or fax from the MDM."

questions.question: Who has operational control on a Flexjet Part 91K flight?

choices.a: The Company and share owner are jointly and individually responsible.
choices.b: All tasks associated with exercising operational control on a program flight are delegated by the owner to the Company.
choices.c: The passenger on board the aircraft.
choices.d: Both A and B are correct.

questions.answer_text: Both A and B are correct.
questions.explanation: On a program (91K) flight, tasks "associated with exercising Operational Control on a program flight are delegated by the owner to the Company" — and both are jointly responsible.

questions.question: The circadian low period is defined by the hours of ___to ___ based on the local time zone where a crewmember’s duty day begins.
questions.explanation: The circadian low is 0130–0400 local to where your duty day starts.

questions.question: The Company defines levels of automation with which of the following terms?

choices.b: Level I, II, III, and IV
choices.c: CAMI

questions.explanation: The three automation levels are Manual, Shared, and Auto-flight.

questions.question: Crewmembers will not donate blood within ___ hours of reporting for duty.
questions.explanation: You can't donate blood within 72 hours of reporting for duty.

questions.question: Engine starts and the before taxi checklists may be completed by a single pilot…

choices.b: at the discretion of the PIC.
choices.c: at the discretion of either crew member.
choices.d: only if approved by the FODM.

questions.answer_text: at the discretion of the PIC.
questions.explanation: "Engine starts and the before taxi checklist may be completed by a single pilot at the discretion of the PIC."

questions.question: For all taxi operations, which following statement is true...

choices.a: The PM will have the airport diagram out and available during the taxi.
choices.b: Maintain a “heads up” lookout during taxi.
choices.c: Both pilots must be task free when crossing runways.

questions.explanation: "The PM will have the airport diagram out and available during taxi. Maintain a 'heads up' lookout during taxi." Both pilots task-free crossing runways — all true.

questions.question: The standard DP/ODP or SID climb gradient is...

choices.c: 1.6% net

questions.explanation: The standard DP/ODP/SID climb gradient is 200 feet per nautical mile (3.3%).

questions.question: Non-essential communication in the cockpit is prohibited during the following defined critical phases of flight.

choices.a: All ground operation involving taxi, takeoff or landing, and any flight operations below 10,000 feet AGL except normal cruise flight, and within 1,000 feet of level- off altitude during climb or descent.
choices.b: Any flight operations below 10,000 feet AGL, and within 1,000 feet of level-off altitude during climb or descent.
choices.c: All operations within Class B, C, D, and E airspace.

questions.answer_text: All ground operation involving taxi, takeoff or landing, and any flight operations below 10,000 feet AGL except normal cruise flight, and within 1,000 feet of level- off altitude during climb or descent.
questions.explanation: Sterile cockpit applies to taxi/takeoff/landing, below 10,000 ft AGL except normal cruise, and within 1,000 ft of a level-off.

questions.question: Prior to takeoff, the flight crew will confirm that the altitude selector is set to the initial altitude.
questions.explanation: The departure briefing confirms the initial heading and altitude and that the altitude selector is set to the initial altitude.

questions.question: Acceptance of any IFR departure clearance requires compliance with the minimum TERPS (Terminal Instrument Procedures) climb gradient requirements with...

choices.a: One-engine inoperative to the MEA, MOCA, or other minimum IFR altitude.
choices.c: All engines operating with gear down.
choices.d: One-engine inoperative with takeoff flap setting.

questions.explanation: TERPS climb-gradient requirements are met with all engines operating.

questions.question: For IFR departures, if ATC does not specify any other particular departure procedure prior to takeoff, a crewmember must comply with the departure procedure (DP or ODP) established by the FAA for the airport and runway to be used.

choices.a: True, use of this procedure will provide obstacle clearance, and they are considered the standard IFR departure procedure.
choices.b: False, no specification of a departure procedure in the clearance implies that the crew is cleared direct to the first filed waypoint.

questions.answer_text: True, use of this procedure will provide obstacle clearance, and they are considered the standard IFR departure procedure.
questions.explanation: With no ATC-specified procedure you fly the FAA DP/ODP, which provides obstacle clearance and is the standard — true.

questions.question: In the approach chart you note that the missed approach point is a circled waypoint symbol. This icon indicates that the MAP is a...

choices.c: visual point on the approach.

questions.explanation: "Fly-over waypoints are used when an aircraft should begin a turn to the next course over the waypoint" — a circled symbol marks a fly-over waypoint.

questions.question: What does the acronym CAMI stand for?

choices.c: Confirm, Accept, Manage, Intervene

questions.explanation: CAMI = Confirm, Activate, Monitor, Intervene.

questions.question: When any of the events that requires an incident report occur, or when otherwise required, the PIC (or other crewmember when requested), shall:

choices.a: Immediately notify a Flight Department manager or Maintenance Duty Manager by calling the GCC.
choices.b: The GCC will generate an internal incident report which will provide initial notification to stake holders within the company.
choices.c: Complete an incident report submission listing all pertinent details of the event by logging in to https://www.oneskysafety.com

questions.explanation: When an event requires an incident report the PIC notifies a manager via the GCC and files the report at oneskysafety.com — all of the above.

questions.question: When is the PIC required to do a manual obstacle analysis?

choices.a: A crew is utilizing the “see and avoid” concept in VMC with the following conditions: An obstacle on the departure path cannot be avoided laterally, and an obstacle may impede the emergency briefing plan.
choices.b: For IFR departures from Class G air space for the portion of the departure prior to entering controlled airspace.
choices.c: A VFR flight is being conducted that needs to satisfy Ops Spec C077.

questions.answer_text: A crew is utilizing the “see and avoid” concept in VMC with the following conditions: An obstacle on the departure path cannot be avoided laterally, and an obstacle may impede the emergency briefing plan.
questions.explanation: A manual obstacle analysis is required when using see-and-avoid in VMC with an obstacle you can't avoid laterally that could interfere with the emergency plan. (Official key: answer a.)

questions.question: If a potential discrepancy is discovered during taxi, the crew should...

choices.a: Comply with section 5 of the FOM and complete the “Discrepancy Discovered After Blockout” procedures.
choices.c: Continue the flight and write up the discrepancy after landing at the destination.
choices.d: Ignore the item and hope it goes away.

questions.answer_text: Comply with section 5 of the FOM and complete the “Discrepancy Discovered After Blockout” procedures.
questions.explanation: A discrepancy found during taxi follows the Section 5 'Discovered After Block Out' procedure.

questions.question: When preparing the aircraft for a live leg, which of the following statements regarding the crewmembers proper actions is true?

choices.a: The lavatory shall be checked for servicing, functionality, freshness and appearance.
choices.b: All trash shall be removed from the aircraft prior to each flight.
choices.c: Each seatbelt should be arranged in a crossed pattern on the seat with any excess belt material neatly tucked within the seat.
choices.d: Sit in the lead passenger seat and inspect the aircraft from the passenger perspective.

questions.explanation: All the listed live-leg cabin-prep items are true (lavatory serviced, trash removed, seatbelts arranged, inspect from the passenger seat).

questions.question: The Maintenance Resolution process can be initiated by...

choices.c: Maintenance Duty Manager.

questions.explanation: Any of the listed roles can start the Maintenance Resolution process — all are correct.

questions.question: Which of the following may the crew NOT connect to the onboard Wi-Fi and use during a flight?

choices.c: Company issued iPhone

questions.explanation: "Crewmembers may not use their personal PEDs during flight" — onboard Wi-Fi is only for official business via company devices.

questions.question: An approach that becomes unstabilized inside the 500-foot window requires an immediate go-around unless...

choices.a: The PIC has more than 100 hours in type.
choices.b: The deviations are small and momentary in airspeed, sink rate, glide path and course and only require minor corrections.
choices.c: The pilot flying feels that the outcome is never in doubt.

questions.answer_text: The deviations are small and momentary in airspeed, sink rate, glide path and course and only require minor corrections.
questions.explanation: "The only acceptable outcome of an approach that is unstabilized at or inside the 500' window is a [go-around]" unless deviations are small and momentary.

questions.question: One of the SIC’s duties is to assume control of the aircraft as necessary to avoid a dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: An SIC's duties include assuming control of the aircraft as necessary to avoid a dangerous situation.

questions.question: The emergency briefing acronym TEST stands for...

choices.a: Train for success, Execute your plan, Survive, Time before rescue
choices.b: Type of emergency, Evacuation plan, Signals, Time before touchdown
choices.c: Tell ATC, Estimate landing site, Send for help, Try to communicate
choices.d: Tell Passengers, Estimate time till landing, Speed to minimum, Touchdown smoothly

questions.answer_text: Type of emergency, Evacuation plan, Signals, Time before touchdown
questions.explanation: TEST = Type of emergency, Evacuation plan, Signals, Time before touchdown.

questions.question: Scheduling shall be advised if owners/passengers are more than ___ minutes late.
questions.explanation: Notify Scheduling if owners or passengers are more than 15 minutes late.

questions.question: The Company authorizes an aircraft to be taxied with only one crew member in their seat with seat belts fastened while the other crew member is dealing with passengers.

choices.a: This is acceptable if one or all passengers require additional time during the brief.
choices.b: This is acceptable because one crew member may be assisting passenger with drinks and/or catering.
choices.c: This is not acceptable. Both pilots should be seated with belts fastened. One crew member then can begin to taxi while the other programs the FMS.
choices.d: This is never acceptable. The aircraft will not be moved under its own power until the pre-taxi brief is completed and both pilots are in their seats with their seat belt fastened.

questions.answer_text: This is never acceptable. The aircraft will not be moved under its own power until the pre-taxi brief is completed and both pilots are in their seats with their seat belt fastened.
questions.explanation: "The aircraft will not be moved under its own power until the pre-taxi brief is completed and both pilots are in their seats with their seat belt fastened."

questions.question: If a crewmember requires hospitalization for any reason, another crewmember shall...

choices.a: remain at the hotel and await further duty instructions.
choices.b: accompany that crewmember to the hospital and notify the GCC as soon as possible.
choices.c: remain with the aircraft and await further instructions.
choices.d: Both A and C are correct.

questions.answer_text: accompany that crewmember to the hospital and notify the GCC as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: The other crewmember goes with the hospitalized crewmember and notifies the GCC as soon as possible.

questions.question: No individual shall consume alcohol while on duty or within ____ hours prior to the end of a “required rest” period or “extended rest” period.
questions.explanation: No alcohol within 8 hours before the end of a required rest period (or while on duty).

questions.question: Section ___ of the FOM provides information on Flight Operations.
questions.explanation: Section 4 of the FOM is titled "Flight Operations."

questions.question: A Rest Period is a period of time free of all responsibility for work or duty prior to the commencement of, or following completion of, a Duty Period, and during which the pilot or flight attendant cannot be required to receive contact from the Company.
questions.explanation: "Rest Period – is a period of time free of all responsibility for work or duty... during which the pilot or flight attendant cannot be required to receive contact from the Company."

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE regarding fatigue...

choices.a: a crewmember needs to use countermeasures overcome his/her fatigue such as conversation, caffeine, etc…
choices.b: each crewmember has a duty to decline any assigned flight when they cannot safely operate a flight due to fatigue.
choices.c: a crewmember should only take one more flight assignment when feeling tired.
choices.d: each crewmember should manage assigned rest periods to not become fatigued.

questions.answer_text: each crewmember has a duty to decline any assigned flight when they cannot safely operate a flight due to fatigue.
questions.explanation: "[Each] crewmember has a duty to decline any assigned flight when they cannot safely operate a flight due to fatigue."

questions.question: Trip times in Tailwinds may differ from flight plan times because passenger trips are scheduled in Tailwinds based on Boeing 85% probability annual wind aloft data while flight plans calculate times based on short term forecast conditions.
questions.explanation: Tailwinds times are "predicated on data derived from the Boeing 85% probability annual wind aloft data"; flight plans use short-term forecasts.

questions.question: After landing, checklists shall not be started until...

choices.a: the aircraft has slowed on the landing roll to below 65 KIAS.
choices.b: the thrust reversers have been stowed by the pilot flying.
choices.c: the aircraft has cleared the active runway.
choices.d: the aircraft is stopped on the runway.

questions.answer_text: the aircraft has cleared the active runway.
questions.explanation: "After landing, checklists shall not be started until the aircraft has cleared the active runway."

questions.question: Should the PM (Pilot Monitoring) call out a flight deviation or condition to the PF (Pilot Flying) and there is no response after the ___ challenge, the PM shall verbally announce that he/she is assuming control of the aircraft and take the necessary action to correct the deviation to ensure the safety of the aircraft.

choices.c: third

questions.explanation: If the pilot flying doesn't respond after the second challenge, the monitoring pilot takes control.

questions.question: When flows are authorized in the CFM, the flow followed by the challenge and response method will be used to complete required checklists.
questions.explanation: "When flows are authorized in the CFM, the flow followed by the challenge and response method will be used to complete required checklists."

questions.question: The responsibility for command and control of aircraft is _____ delegated to automation.

choices.c: sometimes

questions.explanation: The crew keeps "responsibility for command and control of the aircraft flight path; this responsibility is never delegated to automation."

questions.question: The practice of loading the flight plan route prior to picking up the ATC clearance is…

choices.b: encouraged because it helps the crew get ahead.
choices.c: encouraged but should never be placed in the primary FMS.
choices.d: encouraged because you can review fixes along the route.

questions.explanation: Loading the flight-plan route before you have the ATC clearance is discouraged.

questions.question: VFR charts (electronic or paper) are required onboard an aircraft...

choices.b: only when VFR operations are conducted.
choices.c: never because we have IFR charts.
choices.d: never because we do not operate VFR.

questions.answer_text: only when VFR operations are conducted.
questions.explanation: VFR charts are required only when VFR operations are conducted — not needed if you're IFR the whole flight.

questions.question: For aircraft without operative outlets installed in the cockpit, minimum dispatch battery power available (at block out) as indicated on the iPad is___. If below ___ on either EFB, paper approach charts must be printed before flight.
questions.explanation: Minimum dispatch battery is 30%; below 30% on either EFB, print paper approach charts.

questions.question: Display of Own-Ship position on approved portable and installed EFB units while on the ground or inflight is required to aid situational awareness.
questions.explanation: Displaying own-ship position (on the ground or in flight) is required to help situational awareness — true.

questions.question: Crewmembers shall discontinue the use of own-ship during ground operations whenever any discrepancies (no more than 30 meters) are observed between the actual aircraft position and the own-ship position display.
questions.explanation: Stop using own-ship on the ground whenever you see a discrepancy (within 30 meters) between the actual and displayed position — true.

questions.question: A runway is considered as “wet” when it is well soaked but without significant areas of standing water. A runway is considered well soaked when there is sufficient moisture on the runway surface to cause it to appear reflective.
questions.explanation: A runway is 'wet' when it's soaked and looks reflective but has no significant standing water — true.

questions.question: Runway Condition definitions in the FOM are not intended to, and will not be used to, supersede any applicable aircraft AFM information or limitation.
questions.explanation: The FOM's runway definitions never override the aircraft AFM limitations — true.

questions.question: Any items secured to an aircraft seat cannot exceed the floor loading limitations and cannot obstruct the emergency exit or aisle.
questions.explanation: Items secured to a seat can't exceed the floor loading limits or obstruct an emergency exit or aisle.

questions.question: Flexjet LLC has been designated an “Eligible On-Demand Operator.” This means that during FAR 135 operations the operator...

choices.a: may file to, and begin an instrument approach procedure to, an airport that does not have a weather reporting facility but must file an alternate airport that has a weather reporting facility.
choices.b: may utilize the 80 percent rule for landing when a destination airport analysis has been completed and approved for that destination.
choices.c: may select an airport as an alternate if the aircraft can be brought to a full stop within 80 percent of the effective runway.

questions.explanation: As an Eligible On-Demand operator, all the listed statements are correct.

questions.question: With regard to DAAP operations, a first officer who has logged fewer than 100 hours in their assigned aircraft type shall not conduct any takeoffs or landings under the following conditions...

choices.a: Windshear is reported in the vicinity of the airport.
choices.b: When braking action is reported to be less than “Good” for the runway.
choices.c: When the runway has contamination which may adversely affect aircraft performance.

questions.explanation: For a sub-100-hour FO, all the listed conditions (windshear, braking less than good, contamination) prohibit their takeoff or landing.

questions.question: A Duty Period may be extended, with crew concurrence, when....

choices.a: a delay occurs due to circumstances beyond the control of the company or the flight crew.
choices.b: all the scheduled flight assignments for the Duty Period were realistically planned within regulatory limits.
choices.c: the FODM approves an extension.

questions.explanation: A duty period can be extended (with crew agreement) for delays beyond your control when the day was realistically planned and the FODM approves — all correct.

questions.question: The FODM may only approve extensions to the duty period up to a maximum of…

choices.c: 21 hours for a 4 pilot crew.

questions.explanation: The FODM can approve extensions up to 15, 19, and 21 hours for a 2-, 3-, and 4-pilot crew.

questions.question: Should a crewmember need to be removed from duty due to fatigue, that crewmember shall...

choices.a: Advise the GCC as soon as possible.
choices.b: Contact the Chief Pilot within 24 hours to discuss the circumstances of the fatigue related schedule adjustment.
choices.c: Submit an “Incident” or “ASAP” report within 24 hours.

questions.answer_text: Advise the GCC as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: The crewmember's job is to advise the GCC as soon as possible; the GCC then removes them and generates the report.

questions.question: If an aircraft discrepancy has been entered onto the Form 501 by the flight crew and the crew determines that the entry requires modification...

choices.a: The crewmember my draw a single line through the entire text affected. Initial and date next to the stricken text. Rewrite the entry as required.
choices.b: The PIC, Maintenance Control, and Company management must all agree to the correction before it may be modified.
choices.c: The entire 501 form must be voided out.

questions.answer_text: The crewmember my draw a single line through the entire text affected. Initial and date next to the stricken text. Rewrite the entry as required.
questions.explanation: To fix a 501 entry, draw one line through it, initial and date it, and rewrite it.

questions.question: At least one crewmember, at the controls, must wear, secured and sealed, an O 2 mask above what pressure altitude under FAR 135?

choices.c: Flight Level 250, any time one crewmember has left a duty station.
choices.d: Both B and C are correct

questions.answer_text: Both B and C are correct
questions.explanation: Wear the O2 mask above FL350, and above FL250 any time one pilot leaves the station — both B and C.

questions.question: A rejected takeoff is any action by the pilot that prevents a normal takeoff once the aircraft has been cleared into position for takeoff. If this occurs...

choices.a: The PIC must submit an incident report to the Company within 24 hours.
choices.b: The event will be immediately reported to a Flight Department manager by calling GCC.
choices.c: No action is required.
choices.d: Both A and B are correct.

questions.answer_text: Both A and B are correct.
questions.explanation: A rejected takeoff is reported both ways: notify a Flight Department manager via GCC and file an incident report within 24 hours.

questions.question: A Passenger Safety Briefing shall be given to the passengers on an FAR 91K or FAR 135 trip...

choices.a: for passengers who indicate that they are unfamiliar with the safety briefing.
choices.b: on the first flight of each day.
choices.c: prior to each takeoff.
choices.d: for any passenger who has not flown within the preceding 90 days.

questions.explanation: A passenger safety briefing is required by the FOM and is given prior to each takeoff.

questions.question: What announcements must be made to passengers using the PA system on an FAR 135 trip?

choices.a: “Prepare for takeoff” – when takeoff is imminent.
choices.b: “Prepare the cabin for landing” – approximately 10 minutes from landing.
choices.c: “Prepare for landing” – approximately 2 to 3 minutes from landing.

questions.explanation: None are correct — the PA system is avoided; takeoff, arrival, and landing cues are given with seat-belt signs and cabin chimes, not PA announcements.

questions.question: Entering a runway (active or non-active) for the purpose of crossing or positioning for takeoff, crewmembers shall do the following before crossing the hold short lines:

choices.a: Both pilots must hear and understand the taxi clearance and verbally agree before crossing any runway hold short line.
choices.b: Both pilots must be task free.
choices.c: The left seat pilot must ensure the area on the left is clear and then state “Clear left”. The right seat pilot must check the area on the right is clear then state “Clear right”.

questions.explanation: All the listed runway-entry actions are required before crossing the hold-short line.

questions.question: The flight crew shall maintain ___________ for all flight operations conducted __________.

choices.a: A quiet environment / with passengers aboard
choices.c: Sterile cockpit / only during takeoff and landing

questions.explanation: Maintain a sterile cockpit for all operations below 10,000 ft AGL.

questions.question: A “Land and Hold Short” clearance can only be accepted if the flight crew can assure ATC that the aircraft can be stopped well short of the point specified.
questions.explanation: The company isn't authorized to do LAHSO, so a hold-short clearance can't be accepted — the statement is false.

questions.question: IVSI should not exceed ________ fpm to be considered a “stabilized approach.”
questions.explanation: "The descent rate should not be allowed to exceed 1,000 feet per minute at any time" to be a stabilized approach (IVSI less than 1000 fpm).

questions.question: Prior to takeoff in icing conditions, which of the following statements is true?

choices.a: The aircraft must be free of all frozen contaminants adhering to the wings, control surfaces, engine inlets, or other critical surfaces before takeoff.
choices.b: Always increase rotation speeds to account for the increase in stall speed with ice on the wings.
choices.c: Always make sure that there is approximately the same amount of ice on each wing.
choices.d: Make sure to move the controls forcefully during taxi to break loose any ice that might be binding them.

questions.answer_text: The aircraft must be free of all frozen contaminants adhering to the wings, control surfaces, engine inlets, or other critical surfaces before takeoff.
questions.explanation: The aircraft must be "free of all frozen contaminants prior to takeoff."

questions.question: Regardless of the “Holdover Times,” a pre-takeoff contamination check must be accomplished within _________ before takeoff in ground-icing conditions.

choices.c: 5 minutes

questions.explanation: Regardless of holdover time, do the pre-takeoff contamination check within 5 minutes of takeoff.

questions.question: You are given a braking action report of “NIL” from a G-IV that landed just prior to starting your approach. Upon receiving that report you must...

choices.a: Not takeoff or land on a runway that is reporting “nil” breaking action from a reliable and timely breaking action report.
choices.c: Avoid using the brakes, as they will be ineffective.
choices.d: Ensure that you’re using the longest available runway.

questions.answer_text: Not takeoff or land on a runway that is reporting “nil” breaking action from a reliable and timely breaking action report.
questions.explanation: With a reliable and timely 'NIL' braking report you will not take off or land on that runway.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding anti-icing holdover time (HOT)?

choices.a: Holdover times are revised every year and are located on EFBs and/or the Aircrew Portal.
choices.b: Crew members may reference the Holdover Calculator application by Kilo Lima Management via their Company iPhone.
choices.c: HOT’s are advisory only. A pre-takeoff contamination check must be accomplished within 5 minutes of takeoff whenever operating in ground icing conditions.

questions.explanation: All the listed holdover-time statements are true.

questions.question: After an accident, is it permissible to move or damage an aircraft’s parts or records?

choices.b: Not unless you are one of the crewmembers.
choices.c: Yes, but only if it is necessary to assist persons injured or trapped.
choices.d: Only at the direction of the Chief Pilot.

questions.answer_text: Yes, but only if it is necessary to assist persons injured or trapped.
questions.explanation: You may "remove persons injured or trapped if appropriate" — wreckage may be moved only to help injured or trapped people.

questions.question: In the event of an aircraft accident/incident...

choices.a: Do not give any statement to anyone, including the FAA, until cleared to do so by company management.
choices.b: Do not speak to the media or make any statements regarding the accident/incident to anyone.
choices.c: Do not, under any circumstances, speculate as to the cause of the accident/incident.

questions.explanation: "DO NOT GIVE ANY STATEMENT TO ANYONE, INCLUDING THE FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION, UNTIL CLEARED TO DO SO BY COMPANY MANAGEMENT" — and don't speak to media or speculate.

questions.question: For international operations, a check of passports and other appropriate documents for the international travel is required.

choices.a: True, except that minors do not need proof of citizenship.
choices.c: False.

questions.explanation: "A check of passports and other appropriate documents for the international travel is required" — minors are not exempt.

questions.question: When calculating aircraft weight and balance, the crew may utilize...

choices.c: The crew’s own estimates based upon previous weight guessing experience.

questions.explanation: Weight and balance may use approved average passenger weights or actual weights.

questions.question: Pilot crewmembers will receive an updated weather briefing within ____ minutes prior to landing at the destination.

choices.d: There is no requirement to update weather info. in flight.

questions.explanation: Updated weather briefing within 30 minutes of landing.

questions.question: The appropriate Takeoff and Landing (TOLD) information card is to be completed prior to each takeoff and landing. The takeoff section shall be completed prior to departure. The landing section shall be completed during the enroute phase of flight during the landing assessment check. The only exception to this is a very short leg.
questions.explanation: "The appropriate Takeoff and Landing (TOLD) information card is to be completed prior to each takeoff and landing."

questions.question: During Takeoff and Landing, pilots will be alert for windshear warnings or indications and perform the aircraft specific windshear escape maneuver when applicable.
questions.explanation: On the warning the "PF will execute the manufacturers CFIT escape maneuver and associated memory items."

questions.question: Which of the following is true about thunderstorms?

choices.a: If thunderstorm activity is forecast along the route of flight, the thunderstorm detection equipment must be operational.
choices.b: The aircraft should never be flown closer than 5 miles to any visible storm cloud with overhanging areas because of the possibility of encountering hail.
choices.c: While enroute, crewmembers will avoid suspected “severe” storm cells by at least 20 miles, and it is recommended that all thunderstorms will be avoided by a minimum of 10 miles.

questions.explanation: Avoid severe cells by at least 20 miles and all thunderstorms by 10 miles; "turbulence may be encountered within 20 miles of very strong thunderstorms." All true.

questions.question: Advanced Passenger Information System (APIS) reports must be submitted for each flight...

choices.a: At least 60 minutes prior to departure for all inbound/outbound flights to/from the United States.
choices.b: At least 72 hours prior to departure for inbound/outbound flights to/from the United States.
choices.c: Only for flights designated as “threat locations” by the Department of Homeland Security.

questions.answer_text: At least 60 minutes prior to departure for all inbound/outbound flights to/from the United States.
questions.explanation: eAPIS must be submitted at least 60 minutes before departure to or from the US.

questions.question: When operating a trip into Canada, a minimum of 2 hours (no more than 48 hours) notice is required to inform Canadian Border Services Agency (CBSA) of your ETA using the 1-888-CANPASS number.
questions.explanation: For Canada, give CANPASS at least 2 hours' (max 48) notice — true.

questions.question: On flights along routes utilizing Long Range Navigation Systems as the primary source of navigation, how many “Master Documents” will be kept by the crew?

choices.a: Each crewmember is responsible for their own Master Document so that they may be compared to each other.
choices.b: The Master Document is kept by the GCC.
choices.c: Three. One for each crewmember plus one to be turned into the company.
choices.d: Only one Master Document shall be used on the flight deck.

questions.answer_text: Only one Master Document shall be used on the flight deck.
questions.explanation: Only one Master Document is used on the flight deck.

questions.question: For oceanic operations, each pilot will check clearances against the Master Document, track messages, and plotting charts.
questions.explanation: Each pilot checks clearances against the Master Document — true.

questions.question: You are flying eastbound from Wilmington, DE to Bermuda at FL390, not in radar contact. You request a weather deviation north of course for a thunderstorm. If an amended clearance cannot be obtained from ATC, you should...

choices.a: Deviate around the weather without advising ATC.
choices.b: Advise ATC, and deviate to the north. When 5 from original track, descend to FL387.
choices.c: Advise ATC, and deviate to the north. When 5 from original track, descend to FL380.

questions.answer_text: Advise ATC, and deviate to the north. When 5 from original track, descend to FL387.
questions.explanation: Advise ATC and, deviating north of an eastbound track, descend 300 ft to FL387 when about 5 NM off track.

questions.question: IOM Altimetry Procedures require the crew to monitor the altitude control system and not allow the aircraft to overshoot or undershoot a cleared flight level by more than...
questions.explanation: Don't let the aircraft overshoot or undershoot the cleared flight level by more than 150 feet.

questions.question: The Strategic Lateral Offset Procedure (SLOP) is intended to mitigate wake vortex encounters, and can be applied in U.S. Domestic Airspace without advising ATC.
questions.explanation: SLOP is an oceanic/remote procedure, not for US domestic airspace — so the statement is false.

questions.question: Which document may be referenced for international operations?

choices.c: Oceanic Flight Folder

questions.explanation: All the listed international references may be used.

questions.question: Trips may be conducted under FAR Part 91 for the purposes of...

choices.c: Ferrying and repositioning.

questions.explanation: Part 91 is allowed for training, maintenance tests, and ferry/repositioning — all of the above.

questions.question: Survey-Derived Average Baggage Weights in pounds are as follows: Personal Item ____, Checked Bags ____.
questions.explanation: Survey-derived average weights: personal item 12 lb, checked bag 30 lb.

questions.question: In which document(s) will you find our requirements for Alternate Airport IFR weather minimums?

choices.c: Ground Deicing Program Manual

questions.explanation: Alternate-airport IFR weather minimums are in Ops Spec C055 (C079 is takeoff minimums).

questions.question: Pilots are authorized to depart VFR and pick up an IFR clearance en route if...

choices.a: VFR cloud clearances can be maintained.
choices.b: an IFR clearance is obtained within 50nm.
choices.c: it is not otherwise possible to obtain an IFR clearance.

questions.explanation: You can depart VFR and pick up IFR if you keep VFR cloud clearances, get the clearance within 50 NM, and it wasn't otherwise possible — all correct.

questions.question: What is the lowest minimum visibility that we are authorized to use for takeoff when RVR is not available?

choices.c: ¼ sm

questions.explanation: With no RVR available, the lowest takeoff visibility is 1/4 statute mile.

questions.question: What is the lowest RVR minimum that we are authorized to use for takeoff, when RVR is available?

choices.c: 1600 RVR

questions.explanation: The lowest takeoff RVR authorized is 500.

questions.question: Where is the Ops Spec authorization to conduct operations in RVSM airspace found?
questions.explanation: RVSM authorization is Ops Spec B046.

questions.question: Which of the following instrument approach procedure is NOT authorized?

choices.c: RNAV (GPS) PRM

questions.explanation: RNAV (RNP) / RNP AR is the one not authorized — LDA PRM, RNAV-GPS PRM, and ILS/PRM are.

questions.question: What is the lowest IFR landing minimums authorized for use?

choices.c: 1800 RVR

questions.explanation: The lowest landing minimum is 1800 RVR.

questions.question: When determining the minimum weather to be used for an alternate airport, we may apply the weather minimums that are published on the Instrument approach procedure in the FOR FILING AS AN ALTERNATE section.
questions.explanation: Alternate minimums must be derived from the C055 table (add 400-1 / 600-2), not taken from the chart's 'for filing as alternate' box — so the statement is false.

questions.question: Which flights do Management Specs apply to?

choices.c: Part 135

questions.explanation: Management Specs apply to the 91K program (all its flights).

questions.question: Flexjet is authorized to conduct flights under _________ using the applicable authorizations in the Operations Specifications.

choices.c: All flights

questions.explanation: Under the Ops Specs, Flexjet conducts Part 135 and Part 91 (the 91K program uses the Management Specs).

questions.question: Select the statement that is true regarding operations in RVSM airspace...

choices.a: Aircraft must have two independent altitude measurement systems.
choices.b: Aircraft must have an altitude alert system.
choices.c: Aircraft must have an operational autopilot with altitude hold and the aircraft must have an operational SSR altitude reporting transponder

questions.explanation: All the listed RVSM statements are true.

questions.question: When it is not possible for the flight crew to obtain an IFR clearance to depart on an IFR flight plan, VFR departures are authorized, but subject to the provisions of Op Spec...
questions.explanation: VFR departures fall under Ops Spec C077.

questions.question: Crews are authorized to conduct RNAV (GPS) PRM approaches.
questions.explanation: RNAV (GPS) PRM approaches are authorized — true.

questions.question: Pilots may use weather from which of the following approved sources?

choices.a: The National Weather Services for those United States and its territories located outside of the 48 contiguous States.
choices.b: U.S. and North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) military observing and forecasting sources.
choices.c: A meteorological station, or automated observation weather product, authorized by an ICAO member State.

questions.explanation: All the listed weather sources are approved.

questions.question: Crewmembers are authorized to use MDA as a DA during a non-precision approach as long as certain requirements are satisfied.
questions.explanation: You may use the MDA as a DA when the C073 requirements are met — true.

questions.question: During an operation conducted under FAR 135, who has operational control?

choices.a: The Company and the share owner are jointly and individually responsible.
choices.c: The Company.

questions.explanation: Under Part 135, the company has operational control.

questions.question: What minimums may be used for approach Procedures Using GPS or GPS Wide Area Augmentation System (WAAS) aboard company aircraft?

choices.a: LPV minimums if aircraft is approved.
choices.b: LNAV/VNAV minimums if aircraft is approved.
choices.c: LP or LNAV minimums if aircraft is approved.

questions.explanation: LPV, LNAV/VNAV, and LP/LNAV minimums are all usable if the aircraft is approved.

questions.question: Under Part 135 an IFR flight plan may only be cancelled at an uncontrolled airport...

choices.a: When asked to do so by ATC to expedite another departure from the airport.
choices.b: If crewmembers are in direct communication with an air/ground facility at the destination that can provide airport traffic advisories and information pertinent to conditions on and around the landing surface.
choices.c: IFR must be maintained until clear of the landing runway.
choices.d: When visual reference with the landing surface is established and can be maintained.

questions.explanation: You can cancel IFR at an uncontrolled field only under both conditions b and d.

questions.question: You’re at an airport with an operable ASOS that is reporting a visibility of ¼ statute mile. The airport has medium intensity runway lights and no visible centerline stripes. At this airport, you may...

choices.b: Takeoff only if you are provided with other visual references that will adequately allow you to continuously identify the takeoff surface and maintain directional control.
choices.c: Only takeoff with the delegated approval of flight control.
choices.d: Takeoff only with a localizer on the runway to be used that will allow the aircraft to maintain runway centerline during the takeoff roll.

questions.answer_text: Takeoff only if you are provided with other visual references that will adequately allow you to continuously identify the takeoff surface and maintain directional control.
questions.explanation: You may take off at 1/4 SM only if you have adequate visual references to identify the surface and keep directional control.

questions.question: You’re at an airport that has only one functioning RVR transmissometer on the runway to be used. That transmissometer is reporting 700 RVR. You may...

choices.a: Takeoff since it is above the Company minimums of 500 RVR.
choices.b: Takeoff only if other visual references are available to identify the takeoff surface.
choices.c: Takeoff if you can get a pilot report that is better than the official report.
choices.d: Not takeoff since at least two RVR reports would be required.

questions.answer_text: Not takeoff since at least two RVR reports would be required.
questions.explanation: You can't take off — below RVR 1600 you need at least two working RVR sensors, and here there's only one.

questions.question: Required equipment for operating in RVSM airspace includes...

choices.a: An automatic altitude control system and altitude alert system.
choices.c: One altitude reporting transponder.

questions.explanation: All the listed RVSM equipment is required.

questions.question: Company pilots may carry a tire/wheel assembly with a serviceable tire, provided the tire is not over inflated, and the tire is protected from damage during transport.
questions.explanation: A serviceable tire/wheel assembly may be carried if it isn't over-inflated and is protected from damage — true.

questions.question: Passengers or crewmembers may carry a small medical or clinical mercury thermometer for personal use when in protective cases in checked baggage.
questions.explanation: A small medical mercury thermometer in a protective case is allowed in checked baggage — true.

questions.question: A maximum of _____ pounds of dry ice per person may be carried in the cabin area.
questions.explanation: Up to 5.5 lb (2.5 kg) of dry ice per person.

questions.question: Electric wheelchairs may be accepted for transport. What limitation(s) exist if the battery is considered to be spill-able?

choices.a: The battery must be disconnected and terminals must be insulated.
choices.b: If the battery is removed, it must be stored in a strong container.
choices.c: If the battery is removed the packaging must be labeled with a CORROSIVE label, marked to indicate proper orientation, and marked with the words, “Battery, wet, with wheelchair.”

questions.explanation: For a spillable-battery wheelchair all the listed conditions apply — disconnect and insulate, strong packaging, and a CORROSIVE label with orientation and wording.

questions.question: A current copy of the hazmat manual shall be available on board each aircraft in electronic or paper format. Where do crewmembers find this manual?

choices.b: In Foreflight Documents and in the Flexjet Documents drive
choices.c: In the quick reference handbook (QRH).
choices.d: Flight crew members do not have access to the hazmat manual while on the flight deck and should carry a hard copy in their flight bag.

questions.answer_text: In Foreflight Documents and in the Flexjet Documents drive
questions.explanation: The hazmat manual is in ForeFlight Documents and the Flexjet Documents drive.

questions.question: Small arms ammunition for personal use carried by a crewmember or passenger in his baggage, excluding carry-on baggage, is approved if securely packed in boxes or other packaging specifically designed to carry small amounts of ammunition.
questions.explanation: Small-arms ammunition for personal use is allowed in checked baggage if securely packed — true.

questions.question: Curling irons containing a hydrocarbon gas (example... butane) are a HAZMAT exception. No more than one per passenger or crewmember, may be carried aboard company aircraft provided that the safety cover is securely fitted over the heating element. Gas refills for such curlers are not permitted in checked or carry-on baggage.

choices.a: False, butane is listed on the most current DOT chart, and therefore, may not be carried.
choices.b: False, butane curling irons are no longer being produced.
choices.c: True
choices.d: False, curling irons are not approved

questions.explanation: A butane curling iron is allowed with its safety cover on; gas refills are not — true.

questions.question: One self-defense spray, not exceeding 4 fluid ounces by volume that incorporates a positive means to prevent accidental discharge, may be carried in checked baggage only.
questions.explanation: One self-defense spray up to 4 oz is allowed in checked baggage only — true.

questions.question: Battery powered heat-producing articles (e.g., battery-operated equipment such as diving lamps and soldering equipment) are only permitted in checked or carry-on baggage as long as the heat-producing component, or the energy source, is removed so as to prevent unintentional functioning during transport.
questions.explanation: Battery heat-producing gear is allowed only with the heating element or power source removed — true.

questions.question: Which of the following exceptions to the HAZMAT regulations are permitted to be carried aboard Company aircraft as long as they are carried on one’s person?

choices.c: Lighter fluid.
choices.d: Safety matches and one lighter for personal use.

questions.answer_text: Safety matches and one lighter for personal use.
questions.explanation: Safety matches and one lighter may be carried on your person.

questions.question: Supercooled Large Drops (SLDs) are common in freezing rain. SLDs are particularly dangerous and indicates the real potential for severe icing because...

choices.a: The typical SLD is 100 times larger than a typical cloud droplet.
choices.b: The typical raindrop is the same size of the cloud droplet encountered if experiencing rime ice.
choices.c: SLDs are only dangerous if you have the flaps extended and approaching to land.
choices.d: Hail is likely to be present.

questions.answer_text: The typical SLD is 100 times larger than a typical cloud droplet.
questions.explanation: SLDs (freezing drizzle/rain) can be up to about 100 times bigger than a normal cloud droplet, which is why they're so dangerous.

questions.question: This type of fog is commonly found along the western coast of the United States. It requires a light wind for its formation.

choices.c: Upslope fog.

questions.explanation: West-coast fog that needs a light wind to form is advection fog.

questions.question: What type of fog occurs when an air mass passes over an area of gradually increasing elevation?

choices.c: Upslope Fog

questions.explanation: Fog that forms as air moves up rising terrain is upslope fog.

questions.question: What stage of a thunderstorm would crews most likely encounter hail, heavy rain, frequent lightning, strong winds, and tornadoes?

choices.c: Mature stage

questions.explanation: Hail, heavy rain, lightning, and tornadoes happen in the mature stage.

questions.question: Shower and thunderstorm cells sometimes produce intense downdrafts called downbursts that create strong, often damaging winds. Downbursts can create hazardous conditions for pilots and have been responsible for many low-level wind shear accidents. Smaller, shorter-lived downbursts are called microbursts.
questions.explanation: Those strong sinking winds are downbursts, and the small ones are microbursts — true.

questions.question: Clear Air Turbulence (CAT) is a higher altitude (~20,000 to 50,000 feet) turbulence phenomenon occurring in cloud-free regions associated with wind shear, particularly between the core of a jet stream and the surrounding air.
questions.explanation: Clear-air turbulence occurs at high altitude near the jet stream with no clouds — true.

questions.question: Fronts do not exist only at the surface of the Earth; they have a vertical structure in which the front slopes over the colder (denser) air mass.
questions.explanation: Fronts have a vertical slope over the colder, denser air — true.

questions.question: METAR KCLE 311751Z 27011G20KT 1SM SN OVC002 -01/-03 A2992. What is the intensity of the snowfall according to the Holdover Tables?

choices.c: Moderate

questions.explanation: At 1 SM, -1°C, in daytime, the snowfall intensity is Light.

questions.question: METAR KCLE 311751Z 27011G20KT 1SM SN OVC002 -01/-03 A2992. What is your anticipated holdover time if you use Type I de-ice fluid?
