questions.explanation: For Type I fluid in those conditions (light snow, warm temp) the holdover time is 0:11–0:18.

questions.question: To validate the holdover times of a Type I de-ice fluid, what is the minimum required temperature at the nozzle of the fluid during application?

choices.c: 180 degrees F

questions.explanation: Type I fluid must be at least 60°C / 140°F at the nozzle.

questions.question: The visual glide path of a VASI provides safe obstruction clearance within plus or minus__________ of the extended runway centerline and ____ from the runway threshold.

choices.c: 25 degrees/5 SM
choices.d: VASI provides safe obstruction clearance from anywhere the glide path is discernable.

questions.explanation: A VASI protects you within plus or minus 10° of centerline out to 4 NM.

questions.question: While examining the RNAV approach chart during preparation for the approach briefing, you notice a bold font V shown on the approach course profile view. With regard to this notation you should...

choices.a: Ignore it, as we are not authorized to fly to VNAV minimums.
choices.b: The pilot should not descend below the MDA prior to reaching the VDP.
choices.c: Ignore it, since it stands for Visual Descent Point, and we are not planning a visual approach.
choices.d: Note it, but there is no need to plan for or brief a VDP, it is just recommended technique in some cases.

questions.answer_text: The pilot should not descend below the MDA prior to reaching the VDP.
questions.explanation: The bold 'V' marks a Visual Descent Point — don't descend below the MDA until you reach it.

questions.question: If you see a “negative C” symbol next to the circling minimums on a Jeppesen approach chart, it means...

choices.b: All circling aircraft must land on a specific preferred runway.
choices.c: Expanded circling area for TERPS obstacle protection is applied.
choices.d: Circling approaches are only approved for Category C aircraft.

questions.answer_text: Expanded circling area for TERPS obstacle protection is applied.
questions.explanation: The 'negative/inverse C' means the expanded circling area for TERPS obstacle protection — not 'no circling.'

questions.question: With APPR mode selected and on final approach during an RNAV(GNSS) or RNP approach, without an SBAS receiver that uses WAAS, the course indicator will reach full deflection if off course by...
questions.explanation: Without WAAS, the RNAV course needle reaches full deflection at 0.3 NM off course.

questions.question: Crewmembers are required to keep in their possession when acting as a crewmember:

choices.c: Government issued REAL ID.

questions.explanation: "Crewmembers are required to keep in their possession when acting as a crewmember... Pilot certificate (temporary and permanent), Medical certificate" and a government ID — all required.

questions.question: What is the lowest RVR minimum that we are authorized to use for takeoff Part 91K, when RVR is available?

choices.c: 1800 RVR

questions.explanation: Under Part 91K, the lowest takeoff RVR authorized is 600.

questions.question: According to the FAR’s, above what altitude is a pilot required to wear his oxygen mask if the other pilot leaves the duty station on a Part 135 flight?

choices.d: Pilots are not required to wear an oxygen mask in a pressurized aircraft.

questions.explanation: Under Part 135 you wear the O2 mask above 25,000 ft if the other pilot leaves the station.

questions.question: An approved flotation device is required for each occupant aboard the aircraft. If there are only 6 vests the aircraft is limited to carrying no more than 2 crew and 4 passengers beyond power off gliding distance from shore.
questions.explanation: You need a flotation device per occupant, so 6 vests limits you to 6 people beyond gliding distance from shore — true.

questions.question: If an aircraft is light and Vref will be within a lower approach category, the crew may fly to the minimums of that lower approach category.
questions.explanation: You can't drop to a lower approach category just because you're light — so the statement is false.

questions.question: What indications are given that the crew is allowed to perform an (M) procedure listed in the MEL?

choices.a: The crew is never allowed to perform (M) procedures.
choices.b: The “Flight Crew Deferral Item” column indicates “YES.”
choices.c: Crewmembers may only perform (M) procedures if approved by Flexjet management in advance.
choices.d: Crewmembers may only perform (M) procedures if approved by the FAA in writing.

questions.answer_text: The “Flight Crew Deferral Item” column indicates “YES.”
questions.explanation: You may do an (M) procedure when the MEL's 'Flight Crew Deferral Item' column says YES.

questions.question: A category “C” MEL item must be repaired within 10 consecutive calendar-days excluding the date of discovery.
questions.explanation: A Category C MEL item must be fixed within 10 calendar days, not counting the day it was found — true.

questions.question: During single engine operations, unless otherwise stated in the Engine Out Procedure, pilots should make all turns at 15 degrees angle of bank.
questions.explanation: Unless the engine-out procedure says otherwise, make turns at 15° of bank — true.

questions.question: Which statement below is NOT a Company fundamental principle?

choices.b: Taking a Long Term approach to relationships.
choices.c: Treating Employees as the Foundation of a Service Company.
choices.d: The Company is a Will-Not-Carry HAZMAT operator.

questions.answer_text: The Company is a Will-Not-Carry HAZMAT operator.
questions.explanation: The odd one out (not a fundamental principle) is 'the company is a will-not-carry hazmat operator.'

questions.question: Which of the following describes a “Reporting Culture” in accordance with Flexjet’s Safety Policy?

choices.a: Applying appropriate quality and risk management systems and processes as part of our decision making.
choices.b: Crewmembers shall submit all “other commercial flying” to the Safety Department for each calendar quarter.
choices.c: Employees are expected to raise safety concerns and take the initiative to report hazards, threats, and errors, enabling appropriate and timely safety actions to be taken.
choices.d: When people report deficiencies, expose hazards, and raise safety concerns, there is a clear understanding that it is non-punitive and should be done so without fear of retribution.

questions.answer_text: Employees are expected to raise safety concerns and take the initiative to report hazards, threats, and errors, enabling appropriate and timely safety actions to be taken.
questions.explanation: A 'reporting culture' means employees are expected to raise concerns and report hazards, threats, and errors so timely safety action can be taken.
